cards.text: Friend, the LORD has already spoken through Jeremiah the prophet about Damascus, Kedar and Elam (Jeremiah 49:23-39). Now it's Babylon's turn: this word is about Babylon and the land of the Chaldeans.

cards.question: The LORD says to announce it to the nations, lift up a banner and hold nothing back. What's the big news about Babylon?

cards.text: Captured. And the news doesn't stop at the city. Babylon's false gods get named in the announcement too: Bel and Marduk.

cards.question: In the announcement about Babylon's fall, Babylon's idols come through the whole thing in one piece.

cards.text: Bel is put to shame, and Marduk is shattered. Friend, when the news puts SHATTERED right next to your god's name, it might be time to rethink some things.
And here's how it happens, friend: a nation from the north will come against her.

cards.question: When that nation from the north comes against Babylon, what happens to her land?

cards.text: No one will live in Babylon's land, and man and beast both flee. Then the LORD looks ahead to those days, and somebody's on the road, weeping as they come.

cards.question: In those days, who comes together, weeping as they come, to seek the LORD their God?

answers.text: The children of Israel and Judah
The people of Moab and Edom

cards.text: They ask the way to Zion, the city of Jerusalem, and turn their faces toward it.

cards.question: When Israel and Judah join themselves to the LORD, it's in a covenant that will run out someday.

cards.text: Then the LORD says how they got so lost: "My people are lost sheep; their shepherds have led them astray…" Mountain to hill they wander, like following a GPS that sends you the wrong way at every turn until you're three towns past where you started.

cards.question: After all that wandering, the LORD's lost sheep have forgotten their ___ place.

cards.text: Anyone who finds these sheep devours them. And their enemies already have a speech ready.

cards.question: What do Israel's enemies say about devouring them?

answers.text: We're not guilty since they sinned against the LORD
We're not guilty since the LORD gave us their land
We're not guilty since our gods told us to do it

cards.text: Calling that not guilty is like denting somebody's car in the parking lot and leaving a note that says, "You shouldn't have parked there." And even those enemies call the LORD Israel's "true pasture."

cards.question: The LORD tells His people to flee from the midst of Babylon and be like the he-goats that ___ the flock.
The LORD tells His people to get out of Babylon because He is bringing an assembly of great nations from the north against her.

cards.text: Those nations line up against her, and their arrows are like skilled warriors who don't come back empty-handed. Me? I tossed a handful of sprinkles at a bowl across the bakery once, and the ceiling's STILL sparkly.

cards.question: When Chaldea is plundered, the ones who plunder her walk away with barely anything.

cards.text: Now the LORD talks straight to the ones who plunder His inheritance, rejoicing and singing in triumph, frolicking like a heifer treading grain and neighing like stallions. That's a LOUD victory dance in the end zone.

cards.question: Because of all that celebrating, Babylon, the mother of those plunderers, will be the ___ of the nations.
With Babylon left completely desolate, people passing through will stop to admire what's left of her.

cards.text: Then the LORD calls out every archer: line up around Babylon, shoot at her, spare no arrows.

cards.question: Why does the LORD tell the archers to spare no arrows at Babylon?

answers.text: She has sinned against the LORD
She has run low on soldiers

cards.text: Next comes the order to raise a war cry against her on every side.

cards.question: As the war cry goes up all around her, what does Babylon do?

answers.text: She throws up her hands in surrender
She calls on her allies for help
She fires back from her high towers

cards.text: Her towers have fallen and her walls are torn down. That's my twelve-box cookie tower the day I built it on a wobbly counter and called it a display.

cards.question: This is the vengeance of the LORD: as Babylon has done, do the ___ to her.

cards.text: Then comes another command: cut off the sower from Babylon, and the one who wields the sickle at harvest time.

cards.question: With the sower and the reaper cut off from Babylon, the LORD says that in the face of the oppressor's sword, each one will turn to his own people and flee to his own land.

cards.text: Then the LORD tells Israel's story in one picture: "Israel is a scattered flock, chased away by lions."

cards.question: In the LORD's picture of Israel as a scattered flock, which king does He name as the first to devour Israel?

cards.text: And the last to crush Israel's bones was Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon. So now the LORD of Hosts, the God of Israel, has something to say about that king.

cards.question: The LORD says He will punish the king of Babylon and his land just as He punished the king of Assyria.

cards.text: Then the scattered flock comes home. The LORD will return Israel to his pasture, to graze on Carmel and Bashan.

cards.question: Back home on the hills of Ephraim and Gilead, how does Israel's soul end up?

cards.text: From lost sheep to a satisfied soul, friend, I know that kind of trip: one night I'm stuck in a junk drawer next to dead batteries, and in a blink I've got a whole planet and a sky to myself. But one question's left, because in those days the LORD says a search will be made for Israel's guilt.

cards.question: In those days, says the LORD, a search will be made for Israel's guilt, but there will be ___.

cards.text: Judah's sins won't be found either, because the LORD says, "I will forgive the remnant I preserve." And trust me, friend, this word against Babylon is just getting started.
